emma: quick heads-up — ran a perf sweep on Llama-2-70b with MQA/GQA kv configs. throughput dropped ~12% when num_key_value_heads=16 and seq_len doubled. hypothesis: RoPE scaling + kernel fallback + paged-KV fragmentation. anyone seen similar?

raj: can you paste the exact config + a tiny profiler dump? curious if it's kernel selection or memcpy hotspot.

emma: config I used: ```
model: llama-2-70b
num_key_value_heads: 16
kv_dim: 128
page_size: 256
batching_policy: latency_target_ms:50
kernel_preference: auto
roPE_scale: 1.0
```
profiler snippet: ```
GPU total token ms: 78.4
attention kernel: 41.2ms (fused_v1 fallback on some layers)
memcpy (KV paging): 9.7ms
other kernels: 18.5ms
````

olivia: ah — fused_v1 fallback is suspicious. we've seen fused->generic matmul fallback when head layout isn't 32-aligned. with num_kv_heads=16 + kv_dim=128 the per-head dim is 8, so some kernels bail. try `KERNEL_OVERRIDE=kv_fused_v2` to force the new layout-aware kernel. also bump `page_size` to 1024 to reduce fragmentation.

liam: fragmentation note: paged KV with page_size=256 -> high frag ratio for mixed seq lengths. increases extra memcpy and pointer chasing. on our tests increasing to 1024 reduced memcpy by ~60%.

emma: repro profile after kernel override + page_size=1024: ```
GPU total token ms: 67.9
attention kernel: 33.1ms (kv_fused_v2 used)
memcpy (KV paging): 3.8ms
other kernels: 18.0ms
paged_kv_frag_ratio: 0.14
avg_pages_per_sequence: 1.05
throughput_delta: +14%
lat_p95_delta: -9%
```

ciara-bot: [perf-regression-detector] notice: deployment 2026-02-12/rollout-62 shows 2.3% latency increase correlated with change set id abc123. Investigating. :mag_right:

raj: nice. can we isolate RoPE scaling? olivia — you mentioned numeric issues with Qwen-style RoPE when scale !=1.0 — was that for certain rotary dim alignments?

olivia: yes — if roPE_scale != 1.0 and the rotary dim isn't a multiple of 64 we sometimes hit kernel precision edge-cases in fp16 kernels. we added a clamp in kv_fused_v2 that avoids pathological freq wrap. recommended: keep roPE_scale at 1.0 for now or use fp32 kernels for scaled RoPE.

liam: practical suggestion for canary: create two kernel variants in the runtime config: one with `kernel_override=kv_fused_v2,page_size=1024` and a control with `auto,page_size=256`. route 5% traffic to canary, run perf harness for 1 hour with varied seq distributions (short/long mix).

emma: will do. repro command I'm running locally: `./run_perf.sh --model llama-2-70b --kv-heads 16 --kv-dim 128 --page-size 1024 --kernel kv_fused_v2 --batch-policy dynamic_prefill --seq-dist mix`

emma: early results look promising but need SRE canary window. tagging @sre for canary window and rollback hooks. :eyes: 

raj: also add a micro-benchmark that toggles head counts (8/16/32) to capture perf cliff points and dump per-layer kernel choice logs. store as artifacts for postmortem.

olivia: one more gotcha — some Mixtral variants have shifted head ordering in the checkpoint -> runtime ends up transposing heads differently which affects whether a fused kernel can be used. add a head-layout normalization step in the loader to avoid this class of fallback.

liam: noted. I'll open a tiny PR to normalize head layout + expose a `--force-head-layout` flag for debugging.

emma: thanks team. next steps: 1) canary with kv_fused_v2 + page_size=1024, 2) run head-count microbench and upload artifacts, 3) add loader normalize step PR. I'll paste the canary playbook after I schedule the window.

ciara-bot: [deploy-bot] scheduled canary rollout: canary-1778459999 -> 1778462000 (5% traffic) by emma.

olivia: sweet. if canary looks good we'll promote and add a runtime opt-in flag for customers who want aggressive page compaction.

emma: making PRs now. will follow up with perf artifacts and a short summary. :white_check_mark:
